exposure: Normal BMI vs. overweight BMI vs. obese BMI
outcome: Failed IOL (defined as CS with cervical dilatation <3 cm)
cohort: Live, term, singleton, cephalic deliveries initiated with IOL
finding: Maternal obesity is associated with a lower Bishop Score, a more difficult induction of labor process, and an increased risk of failed IOL and cesarean section compared to normal weight women.
mod_finding: Obese women are more likely to have a low BS (<5) at presentation, an increased rate of failed IOL, and increased CS rate, compared to normal weight women.
